title.en: Word Forge Workshop: Roots and Precision
title.es: Taller de la Fragua: raíces y precisión

objective.en: Analyze Latin roots, prefixes and suffixes to work out word meanings, then choose and combine words precisely in your own writing.
objective.es: Analizar raíces latinas, prefijos y sufijos para deducir significados y luego elegir y combinar palabras con precisión al escribir.

success.en: I can use word parts to explain what an academic word means.
success.es: Puedo usar partes de palabras para explicar qué significa una palabra académica.

success.en: I can choose the word form that fits a sentence, such as a noun or an adjective.
success.es: Puedo elegir la forma de la palabra que encaja en una oración, como un sustantivo o un adjetivo.

success.en: I can combine two short sentences into one precise sentence.
success.es: Puedo unir dos oraciones cortas en una oración precisa.

success.en: I can revise a word choice so my meaning is exact.
success.es: Puedo revisar una palabra para que mi significado sea exacto.

narrative: Bram's forge also builds the words you meet in science and social studies. Many of them come from Latin roots such as port (carry), struct (build), spect (look) and dict (say). Put the parts together, check the meaning, then use the word where it fits.

scene.alt: A workshop with a glowing forge and shelves of Latin root tiles labeled port, struct, spect and dict. An anvil in the foreground holds a half-built word.

vocab.def: The main part of a word that carries its core meaning.
A word part added to the beginning that changes the meaning.
A word part added to the end that often changes the part of speech.
Exact and clear, with no extra or missing meaning.

items.prompt: Build words from the parts. Forge at least five real words and read what each part adds.

suffixes.meaning: a person or thing that does it

trans|port|.meaning: to carry across, from one place to another

re|port|.meaning: to carry back information; an account of what happened

con|struct|.meaning: to build by putting parts together

con|struct|ion.meaning: the act or result of building something

de|struct|ion.meaning: the act of tearing something down

in|spect|or.meaning: a person who looks into things closely

in|spect|ion.meaning: a close look to check something

re|spect|.meaning: to look back at with regard; to value

pre|dict|.meaning: to say what will happen before it happens

pre|dict|ion.meaning: a statement about what will happen

pre|dict|ive.meaning: able to tell what will happen

items.prompt: Ask Bram about word parts. Pick questions, and write one question of your own.

say: The root carries the core meaning. In 'inspect', spect means look, so the word is about looking.
A prefix goes in front and adds a meaning. Pre- means before, so 'predict' means say before.
A suffix often changes the kind of word. 'Construct' is a verb, and 'construction' is a noun.
What would you like to know about how words are built?

compose.label: Write your own question for Bram

checks.label: Ends with a question mark and asks something

say: I am not sure. You could ask about roots, prefixes or suffixes.
Good. Now build and check some words.

items.prompt: Build the word that matches each definition. Use the meaning of each part to decide.

tasks.ask: Build a word that means 'a person who looks into something closely'.
Build a word that means 'the act of building something'.
Build a word that means 'to say what will happen before it happens'.
Build a word that means 'able to be carried'.

items.prompt: Choose the word whose form fits the sentence. 'The engineer wrote a ___ report: it explained what worked and what to improve.'

options.label: destructive
options.fb: The root and prefix point to 'tearing down'. Does the report tear things down, or help build them up?

options.label: construction
options.fb: 'Construction' is a noun. The sentence needs a word that describes the report.

options.label: construct
options.fb: 'Construct' is a verb. The sentence needs a word that describes the report.

items.why: The report explained what worked and what to improve, so it helps build things up. “Constructive” comes from build and ends like a describing word, which the sentence needs.

items.prompt: Combine these two short sentences into one precise sentence, using at least one word you built and a connector: 'The inspector checked the bridge. The bridge was safe.'
items.purpose: Precise sentences carry more meaning in fewer words.

checks.label: Joins the ideas with a connector (because, which, although...)
Keeps both ideas: the bridge and that it was safe

ladder.model: Model: After a careful inspection, the inspector declared that the bridge was safe for traffic.
ladder.frame: The ___ checked the ___, and it was ___ because ___.
ladder.partial: The inspector checked the bridge, which ___.
ladder.cue: One sentence. Two ideas. One connector.

items.prompt: Revise your sentence so one word is more precise. Replace a general word such as 'good', 'big' or 'thing' with a word that says exactly what you mean, then add a detail.
items.purpose: The editor's rule: a more exact word means a clearer idea.

checks.label: Still uses a word you built
Avoids general words like good, big or thing

ladder.model: Model: Following a thorough inspection, the engineer concluded that the bridge could safely carry heavy trucks.
ladder.frame: I changed ___ to ___ because ___ is more exact.
ladder.cue: Find one general word. Swap it.

stages.title: A word you have not met

items.prompt: A new word: 'subscript'. The prefix sub- means 'under'. The root script means 'write'. What does 'subscript' most likely mean?

options.label: writing above a line
options.fb: Check the prefix: sub- means 'under', not 'above'.

options.label: writing placed under a line or a symbol
a person who writes
options.fb: That meaning would need an ending like -er or -or. This word has a prefix.

options.label: to write again
options.fb: That meaning comes from re-. This word begins with sub-.

items.why: Sub- means “under” and script means “write,” so “subscript” is writing placed under something, like the small 2 in H2O.

endings.title: A precise forge
endings.text: Bram sets the last word into the frame. 'You used the parts to work out meaning, joined two ideas, and chose a more exact word. That is how a sentence becomes precise.'

endings.title: The forge is working
endings.text: Bram nods. 'You built words from roots and used them. Next time, replace one general word with a more exact one.'

skill.en: using word parts to work out what a new word means and choosing the exact word
skill.es: usar partes de palabras para deducir el significado de una palabra nueva y elegir la palabra exacta

talk.en: Ask: 'What new word did you build? What does each part mean? Do you know a word in Spanish that looks like it?'
talk.es: Pregunta: '¿Qué palabra nueva construiste? ¿Qué significa cada parte? ¿Conoces una palabra en español que se parezca?'
